acf.description: The Anaerobic Dairy Digester Program has $10,544,325 available for grants to build, repair or upgrade systems that capture methane from dairy manure and other organic waste. These systems reduce greenhouse gas emissions while producing renewable energy, fertilizer and other useful products.
acf.eligibility:
All projects must meet each of the following criteria:
  • Project cannot be a feasibility study.
  • Project must be located in the state of Washington at or adjacent to an existing dairy.
  • Project must meet all relevant laws and regulations for Washington state-funded public works projects, including but not limited to prevailing wage requirements.
  • Project must measurably reduce greenhouse gas emissions and/or untreated effluent.

acf.description: Washington State Department of Ecology is offering $18.5 million to scrap and replace old diesel vehicles and equipment with all electric vehicles and equipment. Funding is also available to install charging infrastructure to support the projects.
acf.eligibility:
Who is eligible to apply?

  • Businesses licensed in Washington
  • Non-profit 501(c)(3) organizations
  • Public organizations
  • Tribal governments
acf.requirements:
What vehicles and equipment qualify?

This is an opportunity for projects that replace or repower: On road vehicles, class 4-8, engine model year 1992-2017
  • Emergency vehicles
  • Local freight vehicles
  • Vocational vehicles (sweepers , refuse, etc.)
Non road vehicles
  • Forklifts (> 8,000 lb. lift capacity)
  • Cargo handling equipment
  • Yard trucks/terminal tractors

acf.description:
For the Washington State Department of Agriculture (WSDA) to administer a competitive solicitation process to award 
2026 Specialty Crop Block Grant Program (SCBGP) funds for proposals that enhance the competitiveness and increase 
demand of Washington specialty crops. 

Specialty crops are defined by USDA as fruits, vegetables, tree nuts, dried fruits, horticulture, and nursery crops (including 
floriculture).
acf.eligibility:
Eligible organizations include:
  • industry associations
  • producer groups
  • commodity commissions
  • non-profit organizations
  • for-profit organizations
  • local, state, and federal government entities
  • educational institutions
Projects cannot benefit a single commercial product. Projects cannot provide a profit to a single organization, institution, or individual. Recipients cannot use grant funds to compete with
acf.requirements:
A two-phase competitive process will take place to award an estimated $4.7 million dollars.
  1. Phase I, Concept Proposal: Applicants must apply online following the instructions and requirements outlined in the RFP. The deadline to submit a Concept Proposal for 2027 funding is 12:00 p.m. (PST) on November 2, 2026. Late submittals will NOT be accepted.
  2. Phase II, Grant Proposal: Successful Phase I applicants will be invited to submit a Full Grant Proposal.

title.rendered: 2026 National Urban and Community Forestry Challenge Cost Share Grant Program

acf.description: FY26 funding under the National Urban and Community Forestry Challenge Cost Share Grant Program will address Community Tree Resource Utilization. Waste reduction and product creation through the economic use of community tree resources at the end of their life cycle. Whether generated through pruning or removal, community wood “waste” can be turned into useful products that benefit the community, its economy, and its environment.
acf.eligibility:
Eligible Entities

  • U.S. State Government, including the District of Columbia
  • U.S. Territory or Possession Government
  • Federally Recognized Indian/Native American/Alaska Native Tribal Government
  • Indian/Native American
acf.requirements: All applicants must demonstrate a 1:1 match of federal funds to non-federal funds, which may be in the form of cash, services, or in-kind contributions.
acf.contact: For program information contact Nancy Stremple, National Urban and Community Forestry Specialist at SM.FS.nucfac@usda.gov.
